title: Injective acyclicity gives bounded-below base change (Lean split, general coefficients)
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $f:X\to Y$ a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Call a sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda_X$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] *torsion* if its underlying abelian sheaf is torsion [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] (equivalently, every geometric stalk is a torsion abelian group). Assume that for every morphism $g:Y'\to Y$, every cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]

$$
 \begin{array}{ccc}
 X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
 f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
 Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
 \end{array}
$$

and every injective object $I$ of $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ which is torsion, the higher direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] of the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] vanish:

$$
 R^qf'_*\,g'^{-1}I=0\qquad(q>0),
$$

$R^qf'_*$ being the $q$-th cohomology sheaf of $Rf'_*$ applied to $g'^{-1}I$ placed in degree $0$. Then for every such cartesian square and every $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ all of whose cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^n(K)$ are torsion, the derived exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]

$$
 \Ex_{\square,K}:g^{-1}Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf'_*g'^{-1}K
$$

is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et},\Lambda)$. No hypothesis is put on $g$.

proof.text: Choose a bounded-below K-injective representative $I^\bullet$ of $K$ using [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. To apply the stated injective-acyclicity hypothesis for an arbitrary coefficient ring, the representative must be chosen with torsion terms; this is exactly the coefficient-resolution assertion isolated in [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-injective-resolution], whose statement also includes torsion of every inverse-image term $g'^{-1}I^m$.

source.place: Lemma 0A4B, direction (2)=>(1), first paragraph of the converse proof (injective resolution and torsion coefficient devissage), line 18389

proof.text: For each term $I^m$, the injective-acyclicity assumption gives $R^qf'_*g'^{-1}I^m=0$ for $q>0$. Hence each $g'^{-1}I^m$ is $f'_*$-acyclic, and [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] identifies the complex $f'_*g'^{-1}I^\bullet$ with $Rf'_*g'^{-1}K$ after the chosen resolution. Exactness of inverse image and the corresponding resolution identify $g^{-1}f_*I^\bullet$ with $g^{-1}Rf_*K$.

source.place: Lemma 0A4B, direction (2)=>(1), injective-resolution computation of higher direct images, lines 18389-18418

proof.text: The degree-zero proper exchange map is an isomorphism for each torsion term $I^m$ by [lemma-weil-pbc-proper-underived-exchange]. Naturality of the exchange construction makes these maps a morphism of complexes, and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-termwise] identifies the induced morphism after passing to derived categories with $\Ex_{\square,K}$.

source.place: Lemma 0A4B, direction (2)=>(1), termwise proper exchange, lines 18418-18445; Lemma 0DDE, line 18708

proof.text: A termwise isomorphism of the two complexes is a quasi-isomorphism, so the derived exchange morphism is an isomorphism. Equivalently, applying cohomology to the termwise map and using [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology] proves that $\Ex_{\square,K}$ is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et},\Lambda)$.

split_report.summary: Split the injective-acyclicity implication into resolution, acyclicity computation, termwise proper exchange, and derived conclusion. Stacks Lemma 0A4B proves the prime-coefficient route, while the Lean declaration generalizes to arbitrary commutative Lambda and remains sorry; the missing torsion-preserving injective-resolution assertion is therefore a new unsplit node, lem-weil-pbc-torsion-injective-resolution. Mathlib searches found only unrestricted enough-injectives and generic right-derived facts, not the needed coefficient lemma. No Lean files were written or compiled.
